risks.title: Natural Catastrophe Risk
risks.score_rationale: AIG is exposed to potential losses from natural disasters such as hurricanes and earthquakes. These catastrophic events could have significant impact on insurance operations and financial results. Risks are partially mitigated through reinsurance and catastrophe modeling.

risks.title: Terrorism Risk
risks.score_rationale: AIG is exposed to potential losses from terrorist attacks, particularly concentrated in New York City affecting property and workers compensation lines. Risks are mitigated by the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program Reauthorization Act (TRIPRA) and private reinsurance protections.

risks.title: Reinsurance Counterparty Risk
risks.score_rationale: AIG depends on reinsurance to manage insurance risks and capital adequacy. Potential failures of reinsurance counterparties could result in significant unmitigated losses, though this risk is managed through careful selection and monitoring.

risks.title: Credit Risk
risks.score_rationale: AIG is exposed to potential losses from credit defaults of counterparties and investment obligors. Credit quality deterioration could impact financial position. Risk is managed through credit policies and diversification.

risks.title: Regulatory and Compliance Risk
risks.score_rationale: AIG faces potential losses from regulatory changes, particularly regarding capital requirements, reinsurance regulations, and insurance requirements. Changes in regulatory environment could impact operational costs and capital position.

risks.title: Reputational Risk
risks.score_rationale: AIG is exposed to reputational damage from service failures, claims handling issues, or other operational shortcomings. Reputational harm could impact customer relationships and business performance.
